name: solve-js-performance
description: Performance budgets, benchmarks, and optimisation methodology for solve-js
prompt:
You are working on the solve-js project. Performance is the #1 ethos. Know these numbers:

## Current Baselines (after all optimisation phases)

Pipeline (Full Stack):
- Single eval (cold): ~0.60ms / ~1,667 ops/sec
- Single eval (warm): 0.0022ms / ~454,000 ops/sec (254x improvement from Phase 0)
- 50-line doc: ~0.76ms / ~1,316 ops/sec
- 200-line doc: 1.21ms / ~826 ops/sec
- Variable chain (5 lines): ~0.58ms / ~1,724 ops/sec
- 20 inline solves: ~0.63ms / ~3,175 ops/sec
- Re-eval dirty line: ~0.57ms / ~1,754 ops/sec

VM Isolated (Pre-built bytecode, no parsing):
- Simple add: ~0.5µs / ~2,000,000 ops/sec
- Variable access: ~0.8µs / ~1,250,000 ops/sec
- Unit conversion: ~4.0µs / ~250,000 ops/sec

Lexer:
- Simple arithmetic: 0.0028ms / ~357,000 ops/sec
- Long expression (50 tokens): 0.075ms / ~13,300 ops/sec

## CI Regression Thresholds
- lexer:simple_arithmetic: max 0.1ms
- lexer:long_expression: max 1.0ms
- parser:simple_arithmetic: max 0.2ms
- vm:simple_add: max 0.05ms
- pipeline:single_eval_cold: max 1.0ms
- pipeline:single_eval_warm: max 0.1ms
- pipeline:100_line_doc: max 50ms
- pipeline:variable_chain: max 1.0ms
- Global multiplier: 3.0x baseline = FAIL

## Unmet Targets
- Single expression eval (warm): target < 0.001ms (currently 0.0022ms)
- 200-line doc: target < 1ms (currently 1.21ms)
- Variable chain re-eval: target < 0.1ms (currently 0.58ms)
- Zero any types (currently ~15)
- Test coverage > 90% on core modules

## Golden Performance Rules
1. No optimisation without a before/after benchmark
2. No merge if any threshold is breached
3. Micro-optimisations must be proven, not guessed
4. Correctness > speed, always
5. If you can't measure it, you can't improve it

## Key Wins Documented
- Pooled TypedArray buffers (buildInto) — zero per-eval allocation
- Bytecode cache by expression hash — eliminates re-parsing
- Shared VM with reset() — eliminates VM construction per eval
- O(1) token filtering via Set — faster markdown lexing
- evaluateNumber() fast path — skips Value allocation
- evaluateIncremental() — only re-eval dirty lines via DAG
- Cache consolidation (3→2) — fewer lookups, precise invalidation
- NaN short-circuit — zero-cost guard
